title: Route 53: hosted zones, records, health checks and routing policies

videos.script: A name is the first thing a customer types, and the last thing anybody checks. {{name}} This lesson is about the service that answers for the shop's names, Route 53. {{zones}} You will create two hosted zones. A public one answers anybody on the internet. A private one answers only inside the shop's network. {{records}} Then you write records into them the way AWS wants them written. As a batch of changes, sent at once, that either all happen or none do. {{alias}} One record has a problem. The shop's own name cannot point at a load balancer with an ordinary CNAME. Route 53 has its own answer to that, and it is called an alias. {{policies}} Then the interesting part. Route 53 can give different people different answers. Nine in ten to one server and one in ten to another. Or one server while it is healthy, and a second one the moment it is not. {{moto}} moto stores all of this, and it answers no DNS question at all. So the lesson says, each time, what you saw run and what comes from AWS's documentation. {{price}} And it ends, as the others do, with the price list: what a zone costs, and what a million answers cost. {{end}}
